Seventh-root orthogonality identifies mean sampled sixth power with their squared moduli. The cyclic identity (x+y+z)(x²+y²+z²)−3(x²z+xy²+yz²)=x(x−z)²+y(y−x)²+z(z−y)²≥0 bounds the resonant term by R³/9 after triangle and Cauchy, while U≤R²/3 and V≤R³/27. The resulting 37R³/9 is sharp. Equality forces all three moduli equal and three cyclic resonance phases aligned, equivalent to 7(β−α)≡0 and γ−α=3(β−α), leaving exactly seven projective witnesses. This is a proof for all complex coefficients, not just unit phases or finite samples.
